evidence: src/infrastructure/in-memory-repositories.ts: InMemoryProjectRepository, InMemoryUserRepository and InMemoryTaskRepository implement the domain ProjectRepository, UserRepository and TaskRepository interfaces. The only query filtering is in findByProjectId.

src/infrastructure/server.ts: createApp() builds TaskService from the in-memory repositories and randomUUID, then calls new TaskController(taskService).register(app) and app.use(errorHandler). It is a pure composition root.
src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: input checks live once in the private helpers body(), requiredText(), optionalText() and routeParam(), which every handler reuses.

src/infrastructure/task-controller.ts: errorHandler maps InvalidInputError to 400 and TaskAlreadyDoneError to 409 using instanceof, but finds not-found errors with error.name === "ResourceNotFoundError". This is inconsistent but minor, and the error type is not owned by this module.
parsedVerdict.reasoning:
The three files form one infrastructure adapter layer for the task API, and each has a clear role:
- in-memory-repositories.ts provides persistence adapters that implement the domain repository interfaces.
- task-controller.ts is the HTTP adapter: it parses requests and maps errors to HTTP statuses.
- server.ts is the composition root that wires the repositories, TaskService and TaskController together.

The module uses its own abstractions consistently. server.ts creates the repositories through their classes and registers routes only through TaskController.register and errorHandler. It does not define routes inline or bypass the controller. Each input-checking rule lives once, in the controller's private helpers (body, requiredText, optionalText, routeParam), and all handlers reuse them. The status filter is defined once, in InMemoryTaskRepository.findByProjectId.

One minor smell: errorHandler detects ResourceNotFoundError by comparing error.name to a string. It checks InvalidInputError and TaskAlreadyDoneError with instanceof, so the string check is inconsistent and fragile. Still, that error type belongs to another layer, not this module, so this is not a split into unrelated concerns, a duplicated invariant or a bypass of the module's own abstractions.
